title: Fragments: September 29
author: Martin Fowler (martin@martinfowler.com)
description: Simon Willison: The more time I spend working with coding agents, the more convinced I am that they make software engineering even harder We can do amazing things with them, but unlocking their full potential requires extraordinary discipline and knowledge This has been a constant impression I get from following…
summary: While things like vibe coding get a lot of attention, the real strength of agentic engineering relies on more sophisticated techniques - and these are not easy to learn or execute. takeaways: Those that train the LLM should be responsible for what it does, after all if it has such a galaxy brain it should be able to tell if it’s doing something wrong and either stop or get a human’s explicit approval. ❄ ❄ ❄ ❄ ❄ Dan Davis has 13 theses on agentic AI and regulation .
